description.narrative: Oour Voices Our Futures (OVOF) will use capacity-building and convenings among feminist movements to strengthen and build movements within countries and across regions, while also link feminist movements to relevant actors, such as internet rights’ movements, Dutch allies and progressive policymakers. OVOF believes in strengthening movements from within, to create more inclusive, powerful and resilient movements. To influence laws and policies at national and international levels, OVOF sees this as the only sustainable mitigation strategy in relation to the increasing power of anti-rights and anti-gender forces.

8 initiatives were conducted by eight young feminists, to promote the rights of structurally silenced women. These 8 initiatives ranged from social action projects, to cross-movement dialogues, supporting the development of communication products, as well as supporting the development of accessibility protocols.

CREA continued its engagement with young professionals to create positive social change and impact through work, 10 young feminists were selected and onboarded in July 2024, known as Emerging Leaders (ELs), who have been working closely with CREA's teams, contributing to important programs while gaining valuable hands-on experience. As part of a global community of changemakers, ELs contribute to CREA's mission of advancing sexual and human rights while receiving ongoing support and professional development throughout the program and beyond. The initiative has helped Els understand the nuances and challenges of working within a fast-paced feminist rights organization and develop the skills, networks, and knowledge to drive social change while understanding critical frameworks, perspectives, and management modalities that support social change movements. Els are encouraged to participate in a community of passionate advocates while gaining access to resources, grounded learning, and mentorship for working in feminist social change and advocacy processes. The ELs have been placed in both program and non-program teams across CREA projects, including capacity building, sexuality and disability, SRHR, communications, impact and learning, finance and people and culture teams.

Multistakeholder roundtables by partners brought together survivors of GBV, activists, legal experts, and policymakers to examine the deep-rooted causes, including patriarchal norms, land disputes, and weak legal enforcement and foregrounded survivor testimonies revealing lasting trauma and social stigma of forms of GBV including witch hunting. The discussion served as both a platform for solidarity and a call to action.
